samples.question: The picture is a cream board scattered with small decorative squares - coloured, slate-grey and black - that lie on the bare board and mean nothing. Lying on the board is exactly one thin slate-grey CORD: a single narrow line that runs as a staircase of straight horizontal and vertical runs. It never crosses or touches itself. One of its two ends is covered by a solid black square CAP; the other end is plain. One more solid black square, the RELAY, sits on the cord somewhere in the middle of a straight run, so it is the only black square with cord coming out of two opposite sides; the cap is the only black square with cord coming out of one side. The relay splits the cord into two stretches: the FIRST stretch runs from the cap to the relay, and the SECOND stretch runs from the relay to the plain end. Walk the first stretch from the cap to the relay and write down, at every corner you pass, whether you turn LEFT or RIGHT as you walk. Then walk the second stretch from the relay to the plain end and write down its turns the same way. Left and right always mean left and right for a walker facing along the cord, not up or down on the page. The two stretches always have the same number of corners, and the two lists of turns are identical except at exactly one corner, where the second stretch turns the opposite way from the first. The two stretches leave the relay in different directions, so the second stretch is the first stretch's shape turned to a new orientation with that one turn flipped, and the two lists cannot be compared by sliding one stretch onto the other on the page. A small coloured BEAD lies under the cord at every corner of the second stretch, one bead per corner, and the cord runs across it; no bead lies on the first stretch and no bead lies on the bare board. Find the one corner of the second stretch whose turn disagrees with the turn at the matching corner of the first stretch, counting corners from the relay along each stretch. The answer is the colour of the bead at that corner. Every bead colour is different from the others in the picture, each of the four bead colours is equally likely to be the answer, the disagreeing corner is equally likely to be any of the four, and the answer colour is also worn by decorative squares on the bare board, so no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink identifies it on its own. What colour is that bead? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.
